status: EXPLORATORY / sandbox. Not integrated into paper_b/paper_b.md. Candidate for Paper C extension or v0.5 feature depending on what the Pareto curve shape says. Note on reconstruction: this JSON was reconstructed from the console log of the phase25 run; re-running the script will produce a byte-identical results dictionary (PPL / dPPL / pct all rounded to 3-4 decimals as printed). Key findings summarized in the commit message for 84xxxxx.
key_findings: Pareto curve under qa_nsep_pchan_asym is smooth and monotone in bits on all 3 models -- no kinks, no residual INT4-valley structure.

INT4 valley on Qwen2-7B (naive +1382 dPPL, Table 1 of the NSN paper) is fully neutralized: asym INT3.5 gives +0.085, asym INT4 gives +0.027 (both well below 5 % threshold). The valley was channel-outlier-driven, not bit-grid-structural.

INT2 under asym is NOT catastrophic on these 3 models (8-20 % of baseline), contradicting the companion paper / THEORY.md claim (based on sym INT2) that 'direction needs more than 3 levels'. The asym window rescues INT2 by ~270x on Qwen2-7B (+325 sym -> +1.19 asym).
INT3.5 is a consistent sweet spot: on all 3 models it improves over INT3 by 18-50 % while costing one additional FP16 per 2 channels (effective 3.5 bits/value, 4.57x compression).

INT2.5 is the borderline point: 5.4-9.2 % of baseline across the 3 models, just over the paper's 5 % usability threshold. A 'graceful cliff' rather than a 'rapid degradation' -- the paper's §6.2 wording is slightly overstated under the asym recipe.
